findings.title: EPS run-rate judgment cites the discrete tax benefit but omits the offsetting $1.2bn noncash warrant charge
findings.detail: The Results section says: 'Net income benefited from a large discrete tax benefit in the quarter, so the reported EPS overstates the recurring earnings run rate (our judgment, based on the income-tax note in the 10-Q).' The 10-Q does report a Q3 discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million (income tax benefit of $555 million, ETR (29.6)%). The same filing also reports Other income (expense), net of $(902) million for the quarter. The filing says this was 'primarily driven by the change in fair value of warrant liability of $1.1 billion' and that the company 'recorded a noncash charge of $1.2 billion, primarily related to a loss from remeasurement of the warrant liability'. That pre-tax noncash charge is larger than the $772 million discrete tax benefit and pushes reported EPS the other way. The note uses only one of the two items, so the directional conclusion ('overstates the recurring earnings run rate') is not supported by the evidence it cites, and it may be wrong. The judgment label does not fix a one-sided reading of the filing.
evidence: snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 1441 (noncash charge of $1.2 billion, warrant liability remeasurement)
snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 1481 (discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million)
snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 1726 (change in fair value of warrant liability of $1.1 billion)
generator/note.md Results section, net income bullet
findings.required_evidence: The note.md net-income bullet either names both one-off items (the $772M discrete tax benefit and the roughly $1.1-1.2bn noncash warrant remeasurement charge in other income) and draws a conclusion consistent with both, or drops the claim that reported EPS overstates the run rate. Any amounts cited must be available as {{key}} values or as quotes.

findings.title: Peer TTM period misalignment not noted in peer rationale
findings.detail: The peer EV/Sales leg compares AMD TTM revenue ending 2026-09-26 with peer TTM revenue ending 2026-07-26 (NVDA), 2026-08-02 (AVGO) and 2026-08-01 (MRVL); only INTC ends 2026-09-26. valuation_inputs.json rationales.peers does not mention that the fiscal periods differ (calendar vs fiscal). For fast-growing peers, a TTM that lags by about two months modestly inflates EV/Sales and so the relative leg ($450.35/share). Under the policy bands this does not change the rating: the relative leg would have to rise sharply to move the blended target above -10%. However, the period mismatch should be stated.
findings.required_evidence: rationales.peers (or the note) states each peer's TTM end date versus AMD's 2026-09-26 TTM and says whether the lag biases the median multiple

findings.title: Data-source disclosure omits the earnings-release accession and the price source
findings.detail: The Disclosures section cites only the trigger 10-Q accession 0000002488-26-000191 and the price date. Quotes Q-1 to Q-4 (guidance and demand commentary) come from release_ex99_1.txt, which is from accession 0000002488-26-000188 (snapshot/manifest.json), and the share price comes from the Yahoo chart endpoint (snapshot/prices.json note). Policy section 6 is met because the trigger accession, cutoff and price date are all present. Naming the release accession and the price provider would make the as-of trail complete.
findings.required_evidence: Disclosures line also names accession 0000002488-26-000188 for the release quotes and the provider of the closing price

findings.title: 'All figures ... from SEC XBRL data' overstates the provenance of guidance and price figures
findings.detail: The final disclosure says all figures are generated by code from SEC XBRL data. The Results section heading also tags the earnings release as '(SEC XBRL data)'. The guidance values (guide_revenue_next_q $17.0bn, guide_non_gaap_gross_margin_next_q 55.0%) come from release text quotes Q-1 and Q-2 (values.json sources), not XBRL. Price and peer market data come from the price host. The policy statement itself is present. The wording should limit the XBRL claim to reported financials, or note that guidance comes from quoted release text and prices from the price feed.
findings.required_evidence: Disclosure distinguishes XBRL-derived reported figures from release-quoted guidance and price-feed data
